gotchas.title: Divorce final 02/10/2026; client wants 'Single'
gotchas.trap: File Single because the divorce is final when the return is prepared, or MFS because the agreement says 'separate returns'.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Marital status is tested at 12/31/2025 - still married. But she is 'considered unmarried' (separate return, paid > half of home costs, child lived with her > half year, spouse out of home last 6 months) -> HOH, which also satisfies the agreement's 'separate returns' clause.
gotchas.impact: HOH vs MFS: std deduction $23,625 vs $15,750 + brackets + credits

gotchas.title: Separation agreement: spousal support + child support
gotchas.trap: Report $13,500 spousal support as alimony income (Sch 1 line 2a) and/or child support as income.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Instrument executed 03/20/2025 (after 2018) -> alimony is neither income to her nor deductible by Brian. Child support is never income. Nothing reported.

gotchas.title: Liam released to Brian for 2025 (odd year)
gotchas.trap: Claim both children for CTC ($4,400), or drop Liam from HOH / Form 2441 as well.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Form 8332 releases only the dependency-related credits (CTC/ODC). Megan claims CTC for Nora only ($2,200); she remains custodial parent: Liam still counts for HOH and as a Form 2441 qualifying person (and EIC, though not eligible here).

gotchas.title: QDRO distribution to alternate payee, age 36
gotchas.trap: Report on line 4 (IRA) and/or assess the 10% additional tax ($3,000) because code 1 is shown.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Taxable $30,000 on line 5a/5b (qualified plan). File Form 5329 with exception 04 (72(t)(2)(C) - payment to alternate payee under a QDRO) -> $0 additional tax. $6,000 (20%) withheld on line 25b.

gotchas.procedure_section: OBBBA - no tax on overtime (Schedule 1-A Part III)
gotchas.title: Employer reported the FLSA premium itself
gotchas.trap: Divide the box 14 amount by 3 (as for total-OT W-2s like EVG1001), deducting only $1,620.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Box 14 'QUAL OT PREM' and the employer letter show the premium portion only -> full $4,860 qualifies. Considered-unmarried HOH is not 'married' for 7703 purposes, so the joint-return requirement does not bar the deduction.

gotchas.title: Michigan exemptions after Form 8332 release
gotchas.trap: Claim 3 MI exemptions (Megan + both kids) as in the organizer.
gotchas.correct_treatment: MI personal exemptions follow the dependents claimed on the federal return: Megan + Nora = 2 x $5,800 (assumption stated: Brian claims Liam's MI exemption).

gotchas.title: Grand Rapids resident city return
gotchas.trap: No city return (client's ex-spouse's city has none) or omit the QDRO distribution from city income.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Grand Rapids resident (1.5%) GR-1040R required; premature distribution taxable to the city; tax $1,762 vs withheld $1,311 -> $451 due 04/30/2026.

gotchas.title: Brian's W-2 uploaded by Megan
gotchas.trap: Add Brian's W-2 to her return (or prepare a joint return).
gotchas.correct_treatment: Separate return - Brian's W-2 is not hers; do not import. Keep out of her WP (confidentiality; Brian is not our client).

engine_notes: Itemized deductions $18,486 < standard deduction $23,625; standard deduction used.

software_exceptions.title: QDRO distribution to an alternate payee - 1099-R code 1 triggers a $3,000 additional tax
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: Autoflow put the 1099-R on line 4a/4b (IRA) and, because box 7 shows code 1 (early distribution, no known exception) and Megan is 36, Axcess computed the 10% additional tax ($3,000) on Schedule 2. The 1099-R gives no hint that the payment was made under a QDRO.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Income > Pensions, Annuities and Retirement Plans (1099-R): uncheck IRA/SEP/SIMPLE (it is a 401(k)) -> line 5a/5b $30,000; Form 5329 exception: amount $30,000, code 04 (72(t)(2)(C) - payment to an alternate payee under a QDRO). Additional tax $0. Federal withholding $6,000 (20%) on line 25b.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - a code 1 distribution without an exception code computes the 10% additional tax.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Income > Pensions, IRAs (1099-R): not an IRA; Form 5329 / early-distribution exception = 04 (QDRO) on the full $30,000 (field per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.notes: The exception would have been lost had she rolled the money to an IRA first and then withdrawn it.

software_exceptions.title: Form 8332 release - Liam stays on the return for HOH and Form 2441 but not for the CTC
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: A child entered on the Dependents input with normal codes gets the child tax credit. Deleting Liam to stop the CTC also removes him as Megan's HOH qualifying person and Form 2441 qualifying person (limit drops to $3,000).
software_exceptions.axcess_override: General > Dependents, Liam: keep him with the 'custodial parent released claim to noncustodial parent (Form 8332)' code so he counts for HOH and Form 2441 but not Schedule 8812. Schedule 8812: 1 qualifying child (Nora) -> $2,200. Form 2441: 2 qualifying persons, $5,200 x 20% = $1,040. Do not attach the 8332 (noncustodial parent attaches it) (verify code values in current release).
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - the dependent's 8332 release status must be set so the CTC goes to the other parent while HOH/2441 stay.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: General > Dependents: for Liam set 'Custodial parent released claim (8332)' / not claimed for CTC; keep as qualifying person for HOH and dependent care (field per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.efile_impact: None (duplicate-dependent reject risk if both parents claim Liam's CTC)

software_exceptions.title: Qualified overtime - W-2 box 14 already shows only the FLSA premium
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: The Schedule 1-A overtime deduction is driven by the amount entered as qualified overtime compensation. The software cannot tell whether box 14 is total overtime pay (divide by 3 for the half-time premium) or the premium itself; the firm's EVG1001 workaround (1/3 of box 14) applied here deducts only $1,620.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Wages (W-2) > box 14 / Schedule 1-A qualified overtime input: $4,860 (box 14 'QUAL OT PREM' + employer letter: 162 OT hours x $30 half-time). MAGI $118,662 < $150,000 - no phase-out. HOH (considered unmarried under 7703(b)) - joint-return requirement does not apply (verify field path in current release).
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - the qualified overtime amount is whatever is entered; no inference from box 14 labels.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Wages (W-2) / Schedule 1-A input: qualified overtime compensation = 4,860 (screen/field per current release - verify).

software_exceptions.title: Michigan exemptions count the released child (Liam) because he is still on the federal dependent input
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: Liam must stay on the federal Dependents input (HOH / Form 2441), and the MI return counts dependents from that input, so it can claim 3 exemptions (Megan + Nora + Liam) - $5,800 more than allowed, MI tax $247 too low.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Michigan > Exemptions: override number of dependents/exemptions to 2 x $5,800 = $11,600 (Megan + Nora). Assumption documented: MI exemption follows the federal dependency claim, which Brian takes for Liam in odd years. MI tax $4,550, refund $175 (verify field path in current release).
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same risk - the state exemption count is derived from the federal dependents unless overridden on the MI screen.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Michigan return > exemptions: override to 2 (screen/field per current release - verify).

software_exceptions.title: Grand Rapids GR-1040R - premature QDRO distribution is city-taxable, not an exempt pension
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: Michigan cities exclude pensions/retirement benefits, so a 1099-R treated as a pension on the city input drops out of city income. A code 1 premature distribution is not a retirement benefit for the city and is taxable. The draft excluded the $30,000 (review point 7) - the city return then shows about $1 due instead of $451.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Michigan > City (Grand Rapids resident GR-1040R): include the $30,000 1099-R (code 1 premature distribution) in city income; wages + interest + distribution - 2 x $600 exemptions = $117,462 x 1.5% = $1,762 vs withheld $1,311 -> $451 due 04/30/2026 (verify field path in current release).
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: City return support and its pension-exclusion logic vary by release - verify that the 1099-R is included as city-taxable.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Grand Rapids city return input (if supported in current release - verify): mark the 1099-R as taxable to the city; otherwise prepare GR-1040R outside the package.
software_exceptions.efile_impact: GR-1040R e-filed 03/26/2026; balance $451 by direct debit
